title: SRE: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Error Budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiative process, incident review standards, operational tooling, and canonical runbook structure. It codifies who owns SLOs, how error budgets are consumed and managed, how capacity is planned and validated, and how post-incident reviews are performed. Use this page as the source of truth for SRE practices across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Goals:
- Provide measurable, actionable SLOs for customer-facing systems.
- Tie error budgets to rollout and operational policies.
- Standardize capacity forecasting and scaling tests.
- Ensure consistent incident reviews and remediation tracking.
- Maintain a compact, executable runbook format for oncall.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Overview:
- SLOs measure user-facing success (latency and availability) for key surfaces: API (control plane), Inference Runtime (data plane), and Embeddings.
- All SLO definitions are owned by the service owner (see Ownership section).

Canonical SLO table (examples):

| Service | SLO Type | Objective | Measurement Window | Error Budget | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| api-gateway | Availability | 99.95% successful HTTP 2xx/3xx | 30d rolling | 0.05% | eng-platform-api |
| inference-runtime | P95 Latency (token streaming) | <= 300ms | 7d rolling | n/a (latency SLO) | eng-serving-runtime |
| embeddings-service | Availability | 99.9% | 30d rolling | 0.1% | eng-serving-runtime |

Notes:
- Availability SLOs are based on user-visible errors (5xx or 4xx for legitimate client errors excluded) measured in front of the customer-facing LB.
- Latency SLOs are measured at the serving tier after routing and caching decisions. For streaming responses, use P95 for first-byte and median for steady-state token latency.

Error budget policies:
- When a service exceeds 25% of its monthly error budget, the owner must:
  1) Open an "error-budget-consumption" ticket, link to the SLO dashboard, and notify stakeholders.
  2) Pause risky rollouts and evaluate mitigations (traffic shaping, additional capacity, degrade non-critical features).
- If >50% of budget consumed within a 7-day window, the SRE org schedules a mitigation call and enforces a temporary rollback/hold on changes until stability is confirmed.
- Exhausted budget (100%) triggers a formal incident review and an enforced remediation plan with timelines.

2) Ownership and Responsibilities

- Service owner (typically the product or platform team) is responsible for: SLO definition, dashboards, error budget tickets, remediation plan.
- SRE is responsible for: SLO instrumentation (traces/metrics), alerting guardrails, runbook maintenance, capacity forecasting tooling and oncall playbook enforcement.
- Product/Customer Success must be notified when availability SLOs impacting SLA customers are at risk.

3) Alerting and Escalation

Alerting thresholds (recommendation):
- SLO burn rate alert: burn-rate > 3 for 1h (page oncall)
- SLO medium: >=25% of monthly budget consumed (notify via #sre-alerts)
- SLO high: >=50% of monthly budget within 7d (page oncall and schedule mitigation)

Escalation flow:
1) Oncall receives page -> follow service runbook -> if unresolved within 15min, escalate to primary service owner -> escalate to SRE lead after 45min.
2) For production impact affecting enterprise customers, immediately notify Customer Success and Product Security according to the customer notifications playbook.

4) Capacity Planning and Validation

Principles:
- Plan for 3x typical steady-state throughput for short-duration bursts, and reserve headroom for autoscaling lead time.
- Use both statistical forecasting (historical usage + growth model) and scenario-based stress tests (marketing campaigns, region failover).

Required artifacts for a capacity plan (per service):
- Baseline traffic profile (P50/P90/P99 requests per second; token/sec for inference workloads).
- Resource model: CPU, GPU (type/VM SKU), memory, network egress, ephemeral disk.
- Scaling policy: target utilization (e.g., 60-75% for GPUs), scale-up/down cooldowns, max replicas.
- Cost impact estimate for reserve vs autoscale scenarios.

Operational tests:
- Canary traffic ramp: validated in staging and progressively in production with automated monitors.
- Load test cadence: quarterly full-service test and post-major-release test; use synthetic producers that mimic real request distribution (sequence lengths, batching patterns, cache-hit ratios).
- Failure injection: once per quarter run a controlled failure (latency spike, instance termination) to validate autoscaling and fallback routing.

5) Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

Process:
1) Propose initiative (document root cause, target SLO improvement, estimated effort, owner).
2) Triage by SRE council: assign priority, allocate engineering time, and set measurable metrics (KPIs).
3) Run a short discovery (2 sprints) followed by implementation sprints with defined success criteria.

Example initiatives:
- KV cache prefixing to reduce cold-start tokens by 30% (affects inference-runtime latency SLO).
- Adaptive batching to increase throughput by 20% without violating P95 latency.
- Improved tail latency OS tuning and kernel parameter profile for GPU instances.

6) Incident Review Standards (Postmortem)

Template (must be completed for all Sev>=2 incidents):
- Title: short, descriptive
- Incident lead: name
- Severity and impact window: start/end/total user-minutes impacted
- Timeline: bullet chronology with timestamps (UTC)
- Root cause: concise statement
- Contributing factors: list of technical/process contributors
- Detection: how we detected it (alert/dashboard/customer report)
- Mitigation and recovery: immediate steps taken and timestamps
- Remediation and timeline: actions to prevent recurrence, owners, and due dates
- Lessons learned: clear, actionable items
- Follow-up: link to tracking tickets and verification plan

Postmortem rules:
- No blame culture: focus on systemic fixes.
- Publish within 7 days of incident resolution to the incident-review space and notify stakeholders.
- Track remediation progress weekly until verified.

7) Operational Tooling

Minimum tooling requirements:
- SLO dashboards: Grafana dashboards per service with 7d/30d/90d views and burn-rate panels.
- Tracing: distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry) with sampling rules for production.
- Synthetic monitoring: end-to-end probes from each region, including tokenized inference paths.
- Load testing: k6 or Artillery harnesses with shared scenario repo.
- Chaos tooling: controlled chaos experiments (e.g., instance termination, network latency injection) with safeguards.

Ownership and access:
- SRE owns the baseline dashboards and dashboard templates. Service teams maintain per-service variations.
- Access to tooling must follow RBAC policies in security-and-compliance/runbooks.

8) Runbook Structure and Example

Runbook requirements (one per alertable symptom):
- Title (symptom), Pager decision (page vs notify), Owner and escalation list, Preconditions (what must be true), Diagnostic steps (ordered), Mitigation steps (ordered), Recovery verification steps, Post-incident tasks, Links to dashboards and code/config repos.

Example runbook excerpt: inference-runtime-high-latency

Title: inference-runtime-high-latency
Pager: page -> oncall-engineer
Owner: eng-serving-runtime
Preconditions:
- P95 token latency > 300ms for 5m AND burn-rate > 3

Diagnostic steps:
1) Check Grafana dashboard: P95 latency, token/sec, batch size distribution.
2) Review recent deploys (last 30m) via deployment pipeline UI.
3) Check GPU utilization and queue depth (nvidia-smi / monitoring panels).
4) Inspect model cache hit rate and KV-store latency.

Mitigation steps (ordered):
1) If a recent deploy exists -> revert to previous revision and monitor for 10m.
2) Scale up GPU pool by adding one replica group or increasing instance type (follow autoscale playbook).
3) If queue depth is high and batch sizes are too large -> reduce max_batch_size in serving-config and restart the pool.
4) Enable degraded routing: route traffic to a lower-latency model variant if configured.

Recovery verification:
- P95 latency back under objective for 15m and error budget burn-rate reduced below 1.5.

Post-incident tasks:
- Open postmortem using standard template.
- Schedule reliability initiative if root cause requires engineering work.

9) Reporting and Metrics

Monthly SRE report must include:
- SLO attainment per service (30d and YTD), error budget consumption, incidents (count and severity), capacity events (scale-ups, shortages), and active reliability initiatives with % complete.
- Quarterly reliability review with Product and Customer Success for SLA-bearing customers.

10) Appendix: Useful Commands and Links

- Check P95 latency (Grafana panel): link_to_grafana_service_p95
- Revert deployment (CI CLI): ci rollback --service inference-runtime --to-revision <rev>
- Scale GPU pool (kubectl example): kubectl scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=6 -n prod
- Monitor GPU (on-host): nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
- Load-test harness: /repos/load-testing/scenarios/inference-full.yaml
